questions.q: Why is a normal blood (serum) magnesium test a poor way to rule out magnesium depletion?
options: Serum magnesium is only measured after fasting
Only about 1% of body magnesium is in the blood, and it is tightly defended
The test is usually run incorrectly
Magnesium isn't measurable in blood at all
questions.why: About 99% of magnesium is inside cells and bone; serum holds ~0.3% and is homeostatically defended, so it can look normal despite tissue depletion.

questions.q: Where is magnesium's strongest, highest-certainty evidence?
options: Intravenous magnesium as hospital medicine (eclampsia, torsades, fetal neuroprotection)
questions.why: IV magnesium halves eclampsia seizures, is first-line for torsades, and protects preterm babies' brains at HIGH grade — the opposite of what supplements are marketed for.

questions.q: What is the single highest-certainty magnesium indication in the literature?
options: Antenatal magnesium to protect preterm babies' brains (cerebral palsy)
questions.why: The updated Cochrane review grades antenatal magnesium sulfate HIGH: it cuts cerebral palsy (RR 0.71) and severe brain hemorrhage in babies at risk of preterm birth.

questions.q: What does the best evidence say about magnesium for ordinary adult leg cramps?
options: It is refuted — Cochrane and independent trials found it no better than placebo
It works only at very high doses
It works better than any drug
questions.why: The Cochrane review and independent trials were null for adult idiopathic/nocturnal cramps; the one positive trial was manufacturer-funded. It survives only for pregnancy cramps.

questions.q: How does magnesium's deficiency story differ from vitamin D's?
options: Magnesium's dietary shortfall is genuinely real (~half of adults under-eat it), unlike vitamin D's mostly-artifact scare
Magnesium has no deficiency at all
Vitamin D deficiency is the real one; magnesium's is invented
questions.why: Roughly half of adults fall below the magnesium intake reference — a true dietary gap, whereas vitamin D's 'everyone is deficient' was mostly a moved goalpost.

questions.q: Is 'everyone is magnesium deficient' accurate?
options: No — measured deficiency is only ~2–15%; the figure conflates under-eating with clinical deficiency
questions.why: About half under-eat magnesium, but measured hypomagnesemia is only ~2–15% (higher in diabetes ~32%). Under-eating the RDA is not the same as being clinically deficient.

questions.q: What does the 350 mg/day supplemental upper limit for magnesium actually represent?
options: The dose where magnesium becomes toxic
The threshold where supplements start causing diarrhea (not toxicity)
The amount in a typical multivitamin
questions.why: The 350 mg ceiling is set by osmotic diarrhea, not poisoning; food magnesium has no limit because healthy kidneys excrete the excess.

questions.q: Which oral magnesium use is genuinely evidence-based (and under-sold)?
options: Magnesium oxide as a constipation laxative
questions.why: Magnesium oxide (~1.5 g/day) tripled the constipation response over placebo and is conditionally recommended in the 2023 gastroenterology guideline — an osmotic effect independent of magnesium status.

questions.q: Is magnesium oxide 'useless' because it's poorly absorbed?
options: No — absorption is only ~4% but it's ~60% elemental magnesium, so it still delivers some
questions.why: Oxide is inefficiently absorbed but not unabsorbable; and form differences between salts shrink at steady state when taken with food.

questions.q: In whom does magnesium actually lower blood pressure?
options: Mainly the hypomagnesemic and medicated hypertensives — it's ~null in normotensive, replete adults
questions.why: The 2025 meta-analysis showed up to −7.7 mmHg in medicated hypertensives and −6 in the deficient, but essentially no effect in normotensive replete adults.

questions.q: What's the honest picture for magnesium and type 2 diabetes?
options: Higher dietary intake predicts lower risk, but supplements barely move glucose
questions.why: Dietary magnesium robustly predicts lower diabetes risk (−14% per 100 mg/day), but supplement trials barely move glucose and the largest 2026 insulin-resistance meta was null.

questions.q: What has happened to the 'magnesium protects your heart' causal claim over time?
options: It got stronger with every study
Larger Mendelian-randomization analyses drifted to null for diabetes, coronary disease, heart failure and AFib
It was proven by a huge trial
questions.why: An early positive MR was contradicted by later, larger analyses; composite cardiovascular disease is null in dose-response meta-analysis.

questions.q: What's the 'tell' that magnesium's mortality link is partly a healthy-diet marker?
options: Dietary magnesium lowers mortality but supplemental magnesium shows nothing
Both dietary and supplemental cut mortality equally
questions.why: In a 1.17M-person meta-analysis, dietary magnesium tracked lower mortality while supplemental and total magnesium showed no benefit — the signature of a nutrient marking a healthier diet.

questions.q: Is 'more magnesium = lower risk' true above the deficiency range?
options: No — risk is U-shaped and replacement helped only the deficient (in 1.28M veterans)
questions.why: Both low AND high serum magnesium were harmful, and propensity-matched replacement cut cardiovascular events only in the hypomagnesemic, not the replete.

questions.q: A high Magnesium Depletion Score strongly predicts mortality. What does that prove about supplements?
options: Nothing directly — status predicts outcomes, but that doesn't show a pill fixes them (the biomarker-vs-supplement paradox)
questions.why: Depletion status predicts ~2.5–2.9× mortality across cohorts, but — as with omega-3 — a strong status marker is not proof that supplementing changes the outcome.

questions.q: How strong is oral magnesium for migraine prevention?
options: A guideline-level but modest effect (~600 mg/day), with the definitive review still pending
questions.why: Oral magnesium has (dated) guideline-level support for migraine prophylaxis, but doses are high enough to cause diarrhea and the definitive Cochrane review is still only a protocol.

questions.q: What's the state of evidence for magnesium and depression?
options: A fragile signal in already-diagnosed patients only, on small/often-unblinded trials
questions.why: The pooled effect is statistically significant but fragile and confined to diagnosed patients; the most-cited trial was open-label with no placebo.

questions.q: Which of these genuinely depletes your magnesium?
options: Long-term acid-blocking PPIs, diuretics, metformin and heavy alcohol
questions.why: PPIs (OR ~1.43), loop/thiazide diuretics, metformin, diabetes and chronic alcohol are established depleters.

questions.q: Which diabetes drug class RAISES magnesium instead of depleting it?
options: SGLT2 inhibitors (a genuinely useful, direction-reversing effect)
questions.why: SGLT2-inhibitor diabetes drugs increase serum magnesium ~0.07 mmol/L as a class effect and can even correct refractory hypomagnesemia.

questions.q: What does magnesium actually do for sleep?
options: A small, low-certainty shortening of time-to-fall-asleep in older insomniacs — with no change in total sleep time
questions.why: The only meta-analysis found ~17 minutes faster sleep onset in older insomniacs but no change in total sleep time, at low-to-very-low certainty.

questions.q: Is magnesium glycinate specifically the best form for sleep?
options: No — there is zero head-to-head evidence any form beats another for sleep; the reputation borrows glycine's story
Yes, it's the only form that works
questions.why: No trial shows glycinate outperforms other forms for sleep, and the single clean bisglycinate trial was barely significant (p=0.049).

questions.q: How solid is magnesium L-threonate for cognition?
options: Weak — the brain-magnesium boost is rodent-only and every positive human trial is manufacturer-funded/-affiliated
questions.why: No human study has shown L-threonate raises brain magnesium, and there is still no independent human trial — all positives are small and industry-linked.

questions.q: What does the evidence show for magnesium and anxiety in healthy people?
options: Suggestive only in already-anxious groups, at poor quality — unproven in healthy adults
Proven to lower cortisol in everyone
questions.why: The anxiety benefit appears only in already-vulnerable samples and the evidence quality is poor; no effect is shown in replete, healthy adults.

questions.q: Does higher magnesium intake reduce fracture risk?
options: It tracks slightly higher bone density but NOT fewer fractures, and no trial proves benefit
questions.why: Higher intake associates with modestly higher bone density but not lower fracture risk (WHI + meta-analysis), and no RCT shows a fracture benefit.

questions.q: Does magnesium boost performance in athletes who aren't deficient?
options: No — any signal is confined to deficient, older or untrained people
questions.why: There is no good evidence of a supra-physiologic performance boost in already-replete athletes.

questions.q: What's the evidence for magnesium and PMS?
options: PMS mood benefit is unproven; serum magnesium isn't even reliably low in PMS (the better signal is for period pain)
questions.why: A 2025 systematic review found insufficient evidence for magnesium on psychological PMS symptoms; the stronger signal is for dysmenorrhea (period-cramp) pain.

questions.q: What did Mendelian randomization find for magnesium and ADHD?
questions.why: A 2025 Mendelian-randomization study found no causal magnesium effect on ADHD; existing trials are low-quality and confounded by co-administered vitamin B6.

questions.q: What does the 'magnesium boosts testosterone' claim actually rest on?
options: One small 2011 trial with no true placebo, where testosterone rose even in the exercise-only group
questions.why: The claim rests on a single flawed trial plus an in-vitro mechanism; no regulator recognizes a magnesium testosterone claim.

questions.q: What did the best-designed trials of ZMA (zinc-magnesium aspartate) find?
options: A clean null on testosterone, body composition and strength — replicated three times
questions.why: The best ZMA trial found no hormonal or performance benefit, replicated by two independent 2024 crossovers; the only positive study is co-authored by the ZMA patent-holder.

questions.q: Do transdermal 'magnesium oil' sprays and Epsom-salt baths meaningfully raise magnesium?
options: No — the one human cream trial missed significance and the Epsom claim was never peer-reviewed
questions.why: Skin poorly absorbs ionic magnesium; the one transdermal pilot was non-significant on its primary endpoint and a review judged it unsupported. Oral is the evidenced route.

questions.q: Is 'your food has no magnesium anymore because of soil depletion' well-supported?
options: Yes, proven by the famous nutrient-decline study
No — that study never measured magnesium, and declines are mostly lab-method and crop-breeding artifacts
Yes, soil has zero magnesium now
questions.why: The most-cited 'declining nutrients' paper never measured magnesium, and the best critical review attributes apparent declines to method/cultivar dilution, not depleted soil.

questions.q: What's the first move for getting enough magnesium?
options: Eat magnesium-rich foods first — greens, seeds, nuts, legumes, whole grains
questions.why: Magnesium is the atom at the center of chlorophyll; leafy greens, pumpkin seeds, almonds, legumes and whole grains close most of the intake gap.

questions.q: If you do supplement magnesium, what's the sensible approach?
options: A large single dose of an exotic form on an empty stomach
A modest dose (~200 mg), citrate or glycinate, with food, split if it loosens stools
questions.why: Form differences shrink at steady state with food; citrate or glycinate at a modest split dose is sensible, and oxide is fine mainly as a laxative.

questions.q: What's the evidence-based reason to top up magnesium?
options: A plausible intake gap or a depleting condition (diabetes, alcohol, long-term PPI/diuretic, heavy sweating)
Because a form is marketed for sleep
questions.why: Benefits cluster in the insufficient or symptomatic; a genuine gap or a depleting factor is the real reason to supplement — not the marketing claims.

questions.q: Which practical caution matters most with magnesium supplements?
options: Avoid magnesium laxatives/antacids if your kidneys are impaired, and space it from certain antibiotics and bisphosphonates
questions.why: Dangerous magnesium build-up is essentially a kidney-impairment event, and magnesium chelates tetracycline/fluoroquinolone antibiotics and bisphosphonates, so space them by hours.
